task: D73 B-vs-A ownership and narrow IPC array bounds prototype

decision.owner: B/IPC for a narrowly scoped IPC Cangjie FFI parcel-array invariant; A remains the owner for general C/C++ allocation-bound analysis across repositories.
decision.rationale: The target has an IPC-specific semantic chain: nativeParcel ReadInt32 count -> typed array allocations -> indexed typed stores in CJ_ReadRemoteObjectArray, reached by an exported FFI wrapper resolving a MessageSequenceImpl handle. This is sufficiently specific for a B rule only when constrained to that repository, file, and function. A's generic bounds detectors currently emit no result on the single-file vulnerable source; broad arbitrary C++ scanning or classifying CheckReadLength alone would be unjustified.
decision.limits: This is a source-level candidate and narrow prototype, not proof of product build inclusion, attacker reachability through a local Binder route, runtime exploitability, or exact product impact. Do not treat it as a general IPC dispatch vulnerability or claim all issue-summary changes are independent vulnerabilities. Do not count it as a frozen holdout case; manifest remains untouched.

rule.matching_shape: parcel-derived ReadInt32 count, non-positive return guard, count-sized int32_t/int64_t allocations, and typed indexed writes; one root finding across type[] and id[]
rule.check_read_length_policy: CheckReadLength by itself does not report; the allocation-to-typed-store chain is required.

prototype.preservation: Only detector.py/models.py and the two new detector files above were changed for this prototype. Existing dirty analysis.py, test files, fixtures, manifests, and other untracked files were preserved. No A detector, holdout manifest, or test file was modified by this lane.

manual_negative_checks: CheckReadLength-only shape without typed allocation/indexed stores: no result
source_probe.run_type: direct ad-hoc detector probes; no pytest suite run by D73

independent_test_feedback.evidence: Official wrapper FfiRpcMessageSequenceImplReadRemoteObjectArray resolves FFIData<MessageSequenceImpl> and calls CJ_ReadRemoteObjectArray. The vulnerable source allocates count bytes for int32_t and int64_t arrays then performs indexed stores; fixed source scales allocation by element size. Oracle covers count/remaining-byte cases, safe/fixed/unrelated controls, and one label root across type[] and id[].
independent_test_feedback.interpretation: T73's independent tests establish an oracle and source wrapper binding, not production detector dedupe (the then-current detector had no finding). D73's separate direct probe shows one root on vulnerable revisions and none on fixed source.

blockers_and_unknowns: No product build profile or binary evidence confirms the exact source is included in a target product.
The reviewed wrapper proves FFI handle-to-helper source flow but not attacker control of the handle/parcel through a deployed route.
No product runtime or exploitability claim is made; the adjudication is source-level.
The focused T73 oracle has not yet been replayed against this exact prototype as an integrated test; D73 did not add or run tests per task boundary.

closeout_steps.round_3_completed: D73 chose narrow B/IPC ownership and added a repository/file/function constrained prototype; T73 independently supplied a 5-case oracle and official wrapper evidence.
closeout_steps.round_4_only_if_defect: Replay T73 oracle against the exact integration overlay; require one vulnerable root across type[]/id[] and zero on fixed, safe, short-input, unrelated, and CheckReadLength-only controls. Repair only if a concrete mismatch appears, then update hashes.
closeout_steps.if_round_4_passes: Close this source-level lane with the prototype identity and keep product reachability and frozen-holdout eligibility explicitly unresolved/out of scope; do not reopen repeated audits absent a defect.
